Available now in Foundry and soon through OpenRouter: https://lnkd.in/gNh5aW8b | 410 comments on LinkedIn
body_markdown: Satya, I read the full article, and congratulations to Achint Srivastava and the team. The line that stood out is about calibration. The article says applications use confidence to decide when to act, defer, or ask for review, so a 90% prediction should be right about nine times out of ten. The speed and the cost are strong: 35 times faster than GPT-6 Sol, and $0.042 per million input tokens. That makes the threshold a leadership decision, not a technical setting. The use case of agent controls, where the model decides whether to continue, stop, retry, or hand off to a human, makes this concrete. Someone has to set where “act” ends and “ask for review” begins, own that line, and show the board what happened when the model was wrong.The question for every leader adopting a decision model: who owns the threshold?
